title: What guild ordinances record
bodyMd: Historians have often read the multiplication of guild ordinances in late medieval towns as a sign that the guilds were tightening their hold on urban trade. The inference is weaker than it looks. An ordinance records what a guild wished to forbid, and a rule is most often written down when the practice it forbids has become common enough to trouble someone. A run of ordinances against selling cloth outside the market hall may therefore mark not a tightening grip on the trade but a loosening one: the rules multiply as the behaviour they prohibit escapes control. Only where ordinances are accompanied by records of fines actually collected can they be read as a measure of enforcement rather than of anxiety.
